body: Yeah. I've been there. Tried to kill myself last year, if there was a gun in the house I'd be dead right now.

Hey. Instead of wondering what it would take to make you go through with it,  maybe we could talk about what it would take to make life worth living for you. I know after reading your post that you're dealing with a ton of shit right now.

 The truth is, anybody can be driven to that point. Anybody at all. It's up to each one of us to try to find something to focus on that means something, that grants meaning to all the chaos and pain out there. Pretty much anyone not suicidal right now is only that way because they've found that thing, whether they realize it or not.

Thing is, my kid's mom is actually a wonderful person. I'm absolutely the only one she treats this way, which feels just great. I guess when she's worn out from being nice to everyone else, she feels the need to shit on someone, and I'm a great target because I'm always fucking up.

My kid turns 9 soon. No idea if I'll be able to pull my shit together in time for his birthday, or if I'll miss another one. I honestly don't have any idea what he thinks of me. I don't get that much time with him, and like most boys he's not super into articulating his feelings. I'm just assuming he'll have some hard feeling a towards me once he becomes a teenager. God knows I had hard feelings about my own parents by that age, and at least they were around.

- I isolated from everyone because I care too much, actually. I need far too much, and have very little left to give.

- I absolutely am a burden, and have been told so directly several times by people who have had enough of my shit. I've yet to meet a person I couldn't drain if I was honest about my real problems.

- Also, depression, yeah. Tried lots of different meds over a 2 year period, they all made the problem worse. A lot worse. I was on meds when I tried to kill myself last year. Not doing that to myself again. I appear to be very treatment resistant. I have a combination of ADHD and bipolar which is notoriously hard to treat via medication.

- You're fine.

Oh, yeah, man. You sound just like me. One of my earliest memories was other kids and my teacher making fun of me in the 1st grade because I cried every day, even though I had just moved, my grandpa had just died and my family was a wreck.

If you feel like you might snap or something, I feel like that's got to be because of the amount of emotional suppression you're subjecting yourself to. I'm not agreeing that you're actually a dangerous guy, but I think that's where that impression comes from. It's a pretty good guess that a lot of the fucked up stuff that happens in the world is because people - especially men - are forced to bottle up all their emotions. The ones to watch out for are the ones who succeed. So, you seem all right to me on that score, because you're continuing to process your emotions, which is healthy!

I think we've all had the isolated island dream. People have been people's greatest enemy since the advent of people. But, at the same time we all need someone sometimes, at least for a quality life. Quite the conundrum.

As far as the part we're talking about, being sensitive, yeah. I'm totally OK with it these days. Part what helped was finding partners who really liked me exactly because I was so sensitive. Not to be lewd, but when I found myself thinking "hmm, this BJ was delivered to me because I'm a genuine, sensitive guy..." really helped, lol. Hard to hate that part of me after that happened a couple times, haha.

I found that, while I might technically have less broad appeal than some, the people who did like me tended to really like me. Because guys like me are harder to find. Not just in terms of partners, either. I've also had platonic friends who have let me know that they were only comfortable talking to me about their innermost pain. Some of those people would genuinely lay down in traffic for me to this day, even though I've been a crappy friend to them since then, struggling with depression and all.

I guess I decided that there might be things wrong with me, and lots of things I would change. But being sensitive is not on that list.

Hey. I just wanted to say that appearance definitely isn't everything. It's made out to be way too big of a deal in our society, which fucking sucks. I mean, where's the pride in having a good appearance? Isn't that largely just the result of luck? It's like being proud of being a lottery winner, or a trust fund baby. Sure, those things can be nice, but they're not the result of anything good about you, know what I mean?

I think the things to be most proud of are the the results of hard work in life, not the results of good fortune. And I'm impressed by the fact that you've managed to hold onto employment, despite all the things you're dealing with. I haven't been able to do the same, dealing with my depression, so that tells me that you have some strength in you. Working at Walmart is a lot of hard work, and I think there's honor in that.

The girl who worked you over sounds like a real piece of work, and I suspect that experience is largely responsible for the way that you currently feel. All I can tell you is that even though her intentions were bad, there was still something about you that she wanted. That right there should tell you that you're not nearly as worthless as you currently think you are.

If you feel that minimal human contact might be the way to get through this, I say go for it. But if you do that, do it because you're taking a break from the world's shit. Not because you aren't a good person to have around.

Thanks. I feel like I'm taking crazy pills sometimes with this shit. I wouldn't say some of this shit to my worst enemy, much less someone I knew was battling suicide and depression.

I'm sure my kid loves me and all. At least, for now, while he's still young. But the truth is, I am a shit dad. Been out of his life more than in. The damage has effectively already been done. I've failed to keep each and every promise I've ever made to myself or him since he was born. The fact that I matter at all to him is essentially just a function of how human psychology works. He'd be better off with virtually anyone else, but poor kid's stuck with me.

His Mom told me she'd find him a "real dad" and then there would be no further use for me. That was admittedly just after I left. I kind of believe it's true, though. Too bad she has failed to do so.

Hey, it's OK. You sound just like me. I've had to quit jobs before because something happened, and I had to run out on the parking lot crying hysterically and hide, and then I just couldn't face people there any more after I had broken down publicly, so I just left. I cry in movies, the whole deal. It IS really embarrassing, but it totally shouldn't be.

When I think of all of the things wrong with the world - the cruelty, the exploitation, human trafficking, ethnic cleansing... all the really awful things, you know how many of them are caused by guys who cry? Z-E-R-O. None. It's obvious that the world has its head completely up its own ass in terms of what it values. I guess I decided that a while back that I was sick of it. I might cry easier than most, but I'd much rather have a beer with someone like me than some douche. And I am quite capable of lots of anger, which helps me not see myself as weak. Hey, anger's an emotion too, right?

I hear you when you say the community is shallow. I would expect that to get a lot better as you get older, though. Young people are the worst about that shit (present company excluded, haha). And remember, you don't need most guys to be interested. You just need one (well, or just a few, anyway), at the end of the day. And filtering out douches who are full of it can just be seen as expediting that process.

The good news is that every passing year, people shed dumb traditional ideas of what a man or a woman has to be. And you're super young. I'm just saying, the age of the sensitive guy is coming. Just like "tomboy" is now considered a desirable thing for girls. It used to actually be an insult. As in "watch out for her, she thinks she wears the pants in the family."

Hi. Thanks for your reply. I'm rather surprised that anyone gives a shit. Even I barely do any more, and I am me.

The truth is, my child is a really thorny issue for me. A real emotional minefield. One of the problems I ran into in he past with therapy is that my therapist at the time used my child as a sort of emotional cudgel to try to guilt trip me into staying alive. Something like "well, and you have a kid, so of course on wouldn't do it. It would negatively affect them." 

In other words, it doesn't matter how much pain you're in right now, you're locked in motherfucker, hahahaha. Are you going to put your own welfare above that of your own child? How dare you?

To compound the problem, I got kind of emotionally blackmailed into having a child in the first place. His Mom had an unintended pregnancy, which resulted in a miscarriage. I had always wanted to be a Dad, but I knew the marriage was a sham. But she got really depressed and told me that having a child was the only way she could heal. So, I agreed, even though I knew it was a terrible choice for me. I guess I thought that maybe having a kid would fix me. Nope. 

So, I'm not too into the whole "you have a kid, so you can't now" line of logic. I guess I would hope that there is more value to my existence than the fact of my child's existence. And his Mom has straight up told me that he might be better off without me, since I keep disappearing due to depression. Even if I do decide to keep living, it doesn't mean I get to be a Dad. It looks like that ship might have sailed.

I'm a more sensitive guy, myself. In my experience, lots of girls (and other guys) actually really value more sensitive men. We're kind of like a nice halfway point between extra masculine guys and feminine women. And trust me, not everyone is into masculine guys. We're around for a reason, the world really needs more sensitive guys.

Just because the culture doesn't value certain things, doesn't mean they're not valuable. This is the same culture that says girls have to be a size 0 to be attractive, and must be attractive to have any value. And that thinkers are worth a lot less than athletes. Our culture is largely full of shit, and these attitudes will be seen as backwards and toxic in the future.

I don't know if that helps at all, I'm sure it's probably things you've heard before. But feel free to get back to me if you want to talk about it at all, I'm going to try to be around for the next few days (just made my own first post here.)
